liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (1 review): Pigpen's limited keyboards leave a void, filled by improvising guitars driven by straight-ahead drumming [8]
- **We Bid You Goodnight** (1 review): Attendee says someone can be heard starting something at the very end of the final song [14]

## The recordings

- **gd68-11-22.aud.cotsman.10088.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 11 songs; 85 min; rated 3.41/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Hard to hear because it is an audience recording from 1968; Sound quality could be better; Sound is poor; reviewer says a good mix by a skilled person could make it a keeper [3][4][5][11]
- **gd1968-11-22.aud-goodbear.cotsman.21933.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 11 songs; 85 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [2]

## Around the show

- Phil's book says about 300 people sat in a hall holding 6,000; band felt on from the first chord of Dew [4]
- According to Deadbase, this was the day before TC joined the Dead [8]
- Recalls tuning up, drummers rattling paradiddles, PA feedback, and Jerry counting in Dew; Mickey gesturing, Billy holding the groove [12]
- Claims this was Tom Constanten's first show as a band member, though he is not audible [13]
- Attendee says both Mickey and Bill drummed, and estimates crowd nearer 200 than Phil's figure [14]
- Only show where Mickey had the drums to himself, giving an alternate-universe feel [8]
- Only other show with Mickey as sole drummer is 12-7-68, a few days later [9]
- Band changed a lot a few months later, with Jerry discarding some trademark runs [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-11-22.aud.cotsman.10088.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by J Cotsman; source: Audience [1]. Also: Audience tape passed through several generations; edited version with speed correction and normalization of the Goodbear seed, seeded to etree by J Cotsman [1]
- **gd1968-11-22.aud-goodbear.cotsman.21933.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: AUD>MR>C>C>C>CD>SHN [2]. Also: Edited from Teddy Goodbear's shn set: pitch corrected in Sound Forge, normalized, retracked; heavy digital noise reduction likely applied earlier [2]
